clue.text: But this aircraft is not self-banking

definitions.text: But this aircraft is not self-banking

blocks.note: surface reading: an aeroplane that cannot tilt itself into a turn
setter's reading: the craft's name splits as 'self' plus a bank transfer, yet it is no bank at all, just a rotor craft

explanation.walkthrough: AUTO means self and a GIRO is a bank-transfer system, so the name sounds like a self-banking service; the clue says it is really an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An autogiro is an early rotary-wing flying machine with an unpowered rotor and a forward propeller.

clue.text: Conference perhaps starts with a quiet act

blocks.note: taken as written
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
Conference is a well-known British variety of pear

explanation.surface: A conference opens with a hushed performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conference' looks like a meeting but is a pear variety; 'starts with' puts the other pieces in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on stage is to perform or be seen in a role, which is what appear means in theatre talk.

clue.text: Unseats rider, we hear — agonies result

indicators.note: hearing something means judging it by ear, so the word only needs to match in pronunciation

blocks.note: a horse that unseats its rider throws him off

explanation.surface: A horse bucks off its jockey, and painful suffering follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Throes are violent spasms of pain or struggle, as in the throes of death, so they are agonies.

clue.text: Stained glass window which I put up in grating

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top
one part goes inside another, sitting within the bars of the frame

blocks.note: a grille is a grating of bars
as can mean which, as in 'such as'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Behind an iron grating sits a stained glass window, which I have hung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which' can stand for 'as', as in 'such as'; the turned pair with I is lodged two letters into the grating word.
explanation.definitionFit: Grisaille is grey monochrome painting on glass, and a window decorated in that style is itself called a grisaille.

clue.text: True site of the new distribution

blocks.note: real means true, genuine
a site is a location

explanation.surface: The genuine place where something fresh is handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To reallocate is to share out again, so a reallocation is a fresh sharing or allotment of resources.

clue.text: American freight-wagon with buffet carriage?

blocks.note: to buffet someone is to box or strike them
a railway car is a carriage

explanation.surface: A US goods train pulling a restaurant coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet carriage' reads as a dining car, but buffet is the verb meaning to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: In US railway usage a boxcar is a fully enclosed goods van, the equivalent of a British covered wagon.

clue.text: Lady in “The Ring” not recorded

blocks.note: the letter O is ring-shaped
a live broadcast or performance is not recorded

explanation.surface: A woman appears in a staging of Wagner's Ring that was performed live.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like an opera title; they hide a single ring-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a woman's first name, so it can stand for a lady in crossword convention.

clue.text: Paddling in ocean tossed by gravity-force

indicators.note: things tossed about by the waves land in a jumbled order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
g is the symbol for the force of gravity, as in g-force

explanation.surface: Someone paddles a small boat out at sea, thrown about by the swell.
explanation.definitionFit: Canoeing is propelling a light boat with a paddle, so a paddler in such a craft is canoeing.

clue.text: Use reel to angle for bass, perhaps

blocks.note: to reel is to rock or sway
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Advice to an angler: use the reel to land a bass.
explanation.walkthrough: Reel and angle look like fishing tackle and technique; here they are verbs for swaying and fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bass are among the fish that live around rocky coasts, so a bass is one example of a rockfish.

clue.text: Stalwart pit-head mechanic

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: the opening letter of pit
an artisan is a skilled manual worker or mechanic

explanation.surface: A loyal mechanic who works at the top of a mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit-head' looks like the top of a coal mine, but it means the first letter of pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a loyal, committed supporter of a cause, which is what a partisan is.

clue.text: Hampered fieldfare?

blocks.note: surface reading: a fieldfare, a kind of thrush, held back or trapped
setter's reading: fare (food) eaten in a field, packed in a hamper

explanation.walkthrough: A fieldfare is a thrush; split it into field and fare and 'hampered' becomes packed in a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is a meal eaten outdoors, typically carried in a wicker basket and eaten in a field.

clue.text: Browning round in this holder?

blocks.note: surface reading: a Browning bullet or cartridge kept in a gun holster
setter's reading: a round of bread being browned before a fire, held on a long pronged utensil

explanation.walkthrough: Browning is a gun maker and a round is ammunition; here a round is a slice of bread and browning is cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a long-handled fork used to hold bread in front of a fire so it browns.

clue.text: Sandy area near a resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it means sort the letters again into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A beach close to a seaside holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday town; it is re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena's floor was traditionally strewn with sand, and the word comes from the Latin for sand.

clue.text: Album released with free needle?

blocks.note: something released is let loose
a pine needle is the tree's leaf, here one that has come away

explanation.surface: A record comes out with a spare stylus included.
explanation.walkthrough: Album and needle suggest a record and gramophone; a needle is also a conifer's leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose-leaf album or binder has pages that can be removed and added freely.

clue.text: Princess .Gail changed here in mid-continent

definitions.note: 'here' is the place; the phrase locates it

indicators.note: something changed is altered, so the letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: the first set of letters to rearrange
the second set of letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A princess called Gail changed clothes in the middle of a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice Springs is the town at the centre of Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The town of Alice Springs lies in the Northern Territory, close to the geographic centre of Australia.

clue.text: Precise penmanship of chief assistant

blocks.note: right means exactly correct, precise
a person's hand is their handwriting

explanation.surface: The deputy writes in very neat handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is someone's most trusted aide, so right-hand describes the principal helper.

clue.text: Plague of pied mice breaking out

indicators.note: things breaking out escape and scatter, ending up in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A swarm of piebald mice escapes and overruns the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is a widespread outbreak of disease, which is exactly what an epidemic is.

clue.text: PC 30 stretched out, in 2 bad way? Take three tablets together

indicators.note: the cross-reference makes this 'in throes, bad way': letters in agony and a bad state are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
the number written out in full as a word

explanation.surface: A medical note: a constable in a bad way is told to take three pills at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is the cross-reference to the answer THROES, so 'in 2' reads 'in throes'; 'stretched out' asks for 30 spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: A triptych was originally a set of three hinged writing tablets, later three painted panels joined side by side.

clue.text: They are all drawn by settlers

definitions.text: They are all drawn by settlers

blocks.clueFragment: They are all drawn by settlers
blocks.note: surface reading: lots or maps drawn up by colonists
setter's reading: people settling bills, who draw open the cords of a money bag to pay

explanation.walkthrough: Settlers look like pioneers; they are people who settle accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the cords that draw a money pouch shut, and figuratively the control of spending.

clue.text: Equestrienne of spirit, eager to return

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: go means energy or spirit, as in full of go
avid means eager

explanation.surface: A spirited horsewoman who is keen to ride back home.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva of Coventry legend rode naked through the streets on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Godiva is famous for her naked ride on horseback, making her the best-known horsewoman of English legend.

clue.text: Wrong to catch up in this game?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are written from bottom to top

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
to net something is to catch it

explanation.surface: Is it unfair to catch up with someone in this sport?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch up' looks like one phrase, but 'up' alone turns the pieces over.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket game played over a net, so it is the game the clue points to.

clue.text: The last sound from Thermopylae?

blocks.note: surface reading: the dying cry of the Spartans at the famous battle
setter's reading: the final vowel sound of the word Thermopylae, written ae

explanation.walkthrough: Thermopylae was the pass where the Spartans made their last stand; the clue is about how the word ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A diphthong is a vowel sound gliding between two qualities, and the ae ending is classed as one.

clue.text: Island in the river belonging to them

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the others, like an island within a river

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for island
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An island sitting in the middle of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is the possessive pronoun for they, meaning belonging to or of them.

clue.text: “Sort of square sheet” as a figure of speech

blocks.note: a T-square is a kind of square, so T names the sort
on a sailing boat a sheet is a rope controlling a sail

explanation.surface: Calling something a square sheet as a turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: A sheet in sailing is not a sail but the line that trims it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a word or phrase used figuratively, such as a metaphor, which is a figure of speech.

clue.text: Springtime border violence

blocks.note: May is a spring month
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: Fighting breaks out on a frontier in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder and destruction, so it fits violence as a general noun.

clue.text: Party race for subscription

blocks.note: a do is a party
a race of people can be a nation

explanation.surface: A political party running for members' fees.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscription can be a sum given to a cause or charity, which is a donation.

clue.text: Consolidate firm in this location

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Merge the company's operations at this site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective meaning solid, fitting 'Consolidate'; it is a business.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together and form a unified whole, which is what consolidating achieves.

clue.text: Practice areas for drivers may have a little butter in stretches

indicators.note: one piece placed within another, held inside the longer word

blocks.note: spans are stretches of distance or time
a butter is something that butts, such as a goat, and a young goat is a kid

explanation.surface: Driving schools might keep a dab of butter on long stretches of road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the spread but one who butts, a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid-pan is a slippery surface where drivers practise controlling skids.
